html:
An oil company in Baku, on the Caspian Sea, founded in 1879 by the Swedish brothers Ludvig and Robert Nobel. For a time it was one of the largest oil producers in the world.

Robert Nobel came to Baku in 1873 to buy walnut wood for rifle stocks for the family's arms works in Russia. He found an oil boom instead and bought a small refinery. With Ludvig's money and their brother Alfred as an investor, they built a modern business. They laid one of the first oil pipelines, from the fields to the refineries, and in 1878 launched the Zoroaster, one of the first successful oil tankers, which carried oil in its hull instead of in barrels. They also built rail tank cars and storage depots across Russia.

Around 1900 Baku produced about half of the world's oil. The company was a model of scientific management and housing for workers. After the Russian Revolution, the Red Army took Baku in 1920, and the company was nationalised.
sum: An oil company in Baku, on the Caspian Sea, founded in 1879 by the Swedish brothers Ludvig and Robert Nobel. For a time it was one of the largest oil producers in the world.
